svg.title: The hub in a browser
svg.desc: After its check of the files, scripts/check-site.sh runs tests/e2e/hub.mjs on the built website in the Google Chrome of the runner. Every request to the address is answered as GitHub Pages would answer it, with a file of site or its 404 page, the data of the dashboard comes from tests/fixtures/repos.json, a page of a project website is a stand-in, and a request to another server is refused and named. At the width of a phone and of a desktop, in the light scheme, five scenarios run at the same time, each in a browser of its own: the search finds a project website, the old addresses lead to the new folder, the 404 page suggests a project, the live facts fill the cards and the Trust table, and the language switch leads to the German home page. When every one passes, GitHub Pages may publish the website. A scenario that fails names itself, the width and what broke, as an annotation and in the summary of the check docs, and keeps a screenshot and a trace in site/.e2e/, which the artifact website of the pull request holds.
